current_mapping.description: explain the purpose and functions of OSI model and its following seven layers: a. layer 7 Application layer, b. layer 6 Presentation layer, c. layer 5 Session layer, d. layer 4 Transport layer, e. layer 3 Network layer, f. layer 2 Data Link layer, g. layer 1 Physical layer;

stem: The purpose of the OSI model in computer networking is to

options.C: connect the devices using cable physically.
options.D: standardise the way of computers communication.

explanation: The Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) 7-layer reference model standardises network communication functions so heterogeneous hardware and software vendors can interoperate seamlessly.

option_feedback.reason: Antivirus installation is a system security utility task, not the purpose of the OSI networking model.
Connection speed depends on bandwidth and transmission media, whereas the OSI model defines communication standards across 7 layers.
Physical cabling is only one aspect of Layer 1 (Physical Layer); the overall OSI model standardises end-to-end computer communication.

current_mapping.description: explain packet switching and circuit switching;

stem: In packet switching, data packets move by

options.A: staying at one path for speedy transmission.
options.B: following the same path to the destination.
options.C: taking different paths to reassemble later.
options.D: waiting in a queue for other packets.

explanation: In packet switching, a message is broken into independent packets that can route dynamically across different network paths and are reassembled in the proper order at the destination.

option_feedback.reason: Dedicated single-path transmission describes circuit switching, not packet switching.
Packets in a packet-switched network are routed independently and do not have to follow the same fixed path.
Packets are transmitted independently across available routes rather than waiting for all other packets in a single static queue.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between natural and artificial systems with real-world examples;

stem: A forest ecosystem is considered as a/ an

options.A: human-made system to control climate change.
options.B: agricultural process that are managed by machines.
options.C: synthetic structure with no fundamental interactions.
options.D: natural system where living and non-living things interact.

explanation: A forest ecosystem exists naturally without human manufacturing and consists of biotic (living organisms) and abiotic (non-living environment) components interacting continuously.

option_feedback.reason: A forest ecosystem is a natural biological system, not an artificial human-made engineering system.
Machine-managed agriculture is an artificial/engineered farming system rather than a natural forest ecosystem.
Forests are natural organic ecosystems with complex ecological interactions, not synthetic structures.

current_mapping.description: illustrate the Von Neumann Architecture using a block diagram;

stem:
A program running multiple calculations needs faster data access.

Based on Von Neumann’s Architecture, the unit that should be upgraded first is a/ an

options.D: memory.

explanation: In Von Neumann Architecture, instructions and data are fetched continuously from the Memory Unit into the CPU; upgrading primary memory (RAM/cache) directly speeds up data access during intensive calculations.

option_feedback.reason: The Input unit only captures external user/sensor data and does not speed up internal CPU data access during calculations.
The Output unit only displays final processed results after calculations are finished.
The Control Unit directs instruction flow inside the CPU, whereas data access speed is bottlenecked by the Memory unit.

current_mapping.description: describe data communication and its components, i.e., sender, message, medium, protocol and receiver;

stem: If two devices are connected but they are not able to communicate with each other, then the missing component of communication system is the

options.D: transmission medium.

explanation: Even when two devices (sender and receiver) are physically connected via a transmission medium, they cannot understand or exchange data without a common set of rules called a communication protocol.

option_feedback.reason: Both devices are already present and connected, so the sender device is not missing.
The receiving device is already connected; communication fails because there is no agreed protocol.
Since the two devices are already connected, the transmission medium is present.

current_mapping.description: explain the following network topologies emphasising their structure, functionality, advantages, and disadvantages: a. bus topology, b. ring topology, c. tree topology, d. star topology, e. mesh topology;

stem:
Consider the given properties.
• Every node is connected with other nodes.
• It is the most reliable network topology.
• It is the most expensive topology.

Based on the given properties, the network topology is identified as

options.D: mesh topology.

explanation: In a Mesh topology, every node has a dedicated point-to-point link to every other node ($n(n-1)/2$ cables), providing the highest fault tolerance and reliability but also the highest cabling cost.

option_feedback.reason: Bus topology uses a single shared backbone cable; it is the cheapest topology and fails completely if the backbone breaks.
Star topology connects nodes to a central hub/switch rather than connecting every node directly to all other nodes.
Ring topology connects each node to only two neighbours in a loop, not to every other node.

current_mapping.description: discuss the positive and negative impacts of computing on daily life and society with examples;

stem:
Arham, a ninth-grade student, uses social media to share helpful posts. However, he also uses the same platform to bully his classmates.

Based on this situation, what does this example show about the impact of social media on society?

options.A: Social media is dangerous and should be completely banned.
options.B: Online efforts to help others are less useful than traditional methods.
options.C: The power of social media rests in the way people use it, for better or worse.
options.D: The harmful effects of social media are more common than the positive ones.

explanation: Because Arham uses the exact same platform both to share helpful educational posts and to cyberbully peers, the scenario demonstrates that technology is a dual-use tool whose societal impact depends on responsible human behaviour.

option_feedback.reason: The scenario shows both positive and negative uses, not that the platform has zero value or must be banned.
Nothing in the scenario compares online helpful posts unfavorably against traditional offline methods.
The scenario gives one positive and one negative action by the same user rather than proving harmful effects are statistically more common.

current_mapping.description: describe the following steps of the problem-solving process: a. define the problem, b. analyse the problem, c. plan the solution of the problem, d. find candid solutions to the problem, e. select the best solution;

stem:
Read the following actions:
• Find out what the problem asks to do.
• Carefully read the problem to understand it.
• What information can be obtained from the problem?
• Find out requirements for the solution of the problem.

The step of problem solving process in which these actions are performed is

options.D: selecting the best solution of the problem.

explanation: During 'analysing the problem', a problem-solver carefully studies the problem statement, extracts known information/inputs, and determines the exact requirements and constraints for the solution.

option_feedback.reason: Defining the problem only states what the problem is initially, whereas extracting information and solution requirements belongs to problem analysis.
Generating candid solutions happens after the problem requirements and inputs have been analysed.
Selecting the best solution is the final step after multiple candidate solutions have already been formulated.

current_mapping.description: describe the following steps of the problem-solving process: a. define the problem, b. analyse the problem, c. plan the solution of the problem, d. find candid solutions to the problem, e. select the best solution;

stem:
Salar is assigned to solve a problem. He has come up with multiple solutions that produce correct results.

The step of problem solving in which Salar’s action is performed is identified as

options.C: finding candid solutions for the problem.
options.D: selecting the best solution for the problem.

explanation: Brainstorming and formulating multiple workable ('candid') solutions that all produce valid results corresponds directly to the step 'find candid solutions to the problem' (SLO 2.1.3d).

option_feedback.reason: Defining the problem simply identifies the goal and scope before any solutions are created.
Analysing the problem identifies inputs, outputs, and constraints rather than producing multiple complete solutions.
Selecting the best solution narrows multiple candid solutions down to a single optimal choice based on efficiency.

current_mapping.description: draw flowcharts using the following symbols, for the problems mentioned in SLO # 2.2.2: a. input, b. process, c. decision making, d. outputs, e. terminator/ terminal point, f. connectors;

stem:
A statement calculates an average of five integers.

A flowchart symbol that must have the statement is a/ an

options.D: decision symbol.

explanation: Calculating the average of five integers is an arithmetic computation/assignment operation, which is always placed inside a rectangular 'process symbol' in a flowchart.

option_feedback.reason: The parallelogram input symbol is only used for reading data (e.g., READ A, B), not performing arithmetic calculations.
The parallelogram output symbol is only used for displaying results (e.g., PRINT Avg), not calculating them.
The diamond decision symbol is used for conditional branching (True/False comparisons), not arithmetic averaging.

current_mapping.description: write algorithms to address the following types of problems: a. performing arithmetic, b. calculating the volume of geometrical shapes, c. converting from one unit to another unit of physical quantities, d. applying the selection process, e. finding the maximum and minimum from input values, f. real-life problems;

stem:
Consider the given algorithm.

```text
Step 1: Start
Step 2: A = 5
Step 3: B = 4
Step 4: C = A % B
Step 5: X = C + B
Step 6: B = B - 3
Step 7: IF B >= 1 THEN GOTO Step 4
Step 8: Output X
Step 9: Stop
```

The output of the given algorithm is
explanation: In the 1st pass: A=5, B=4 -> C = 5 % 4 = 1 -> X = 1 + 4 = 5 -> B = 4 - 3 = 1. Since B >= 1 (1 >= 1 is True), it jumps to Step 4 for a 2nd pass: C = 5 % 1 = 0 -> X = 0 + 1 = 1 -> B = 1 - 3 = -2. Now B >= 1 is False, so Step 8 outputs X = 1.

option_feedback.reason: 4 is the initial value of B, not the final value of X after the second iteration.
5 is the value of X after only the first iteration, but since B becomes 1 (and B >= 1 is True), the loop executes a second time where X becomes 0 + 1 = 1.
9 would result from adding A + B initially, ignoring the modulo operator (%) and the loop.

current_mapping.description: solve the trace table for a given flowchart.

stem:
Study the given flowchart.

If the input value is 3, then the output value of the flowchart will be
explanation: When A = 3, initially B = 1 and C = 1. In the loop, since B remains 1, C = C * B keeps C unchanged, while the 'No' branch increments C = C + 1 (from 1 to 2, then from 2 to 3). When C reaches 3, the condition A = C (3 = 3) becomes Yes, so it prints C = 3.

option_feedback.reason: 1 is the initial value of C, which fails the condition A = C (3 = 1 is No) and continues looping.
When C becomes 2, A = C (3 = 2) is still No, so C is incremented again to 3.
Because B is never incremented (B stays 1 while C is incremented by 1), the flowchart outputs 3 rather than 3! = 6.

current_mapping.description: solve the trace table for a given flowchart.

stem:
Consider the given flowchart.

The missing values in the trace table (X, Y, Z) are
explanation: Initially X = 5, Y = 3, Z = 2. Evaluating the parenthesised expression first: (Z = Z + Y) sets Z = 2 + 3 = 5. Then X = X + Y * Z = 5 + 3 * 5 = 5 + 15 = 20, while Y remains 3. Thus (X, Y, Z) = (20, 3, 5).

option_feedback.reason: Y is never reassigned in the expression, so Y remains 3 rather than becoming 8.
Multiplication (*) has higher precedence than addition (+), so 5 + (3 * 5) = 20, not (5 + 3) * 5 = 40.
Both X = 40 (wrong operator precedence) and Y = 8 (Y was never modified) are incorrect.

current_mapping.description: write HTML code to: a. create and save an HTML file, b. display a webpage;

I. HTML tags are case sensitive
II. Each HTML tag is surrounded by < >

IV. The last tag in any HTML code is </html>

Which of the TWO statements are INCORRECT?

options.D: III and IV

current_mapping.description: write HTML code to create a table in the webpage with the following table attributes: a. table border, b. border colour, c. background colour, d. table width, e. table height, f. table row <tr>, g. standard data cell <td>, h. header cell <th>;

stem:

Personal Information Table

[ ? ]
```

options.D: <tr> <col>Name</col> <col>Address</col> <col>Contact Number</col> </tr>

explanation: In HTML tables, a horizontal table row is defined first using <tr>...</tr>, and each bold column header cell inside that row is defined using <th>...</th>.

Nesting <tr> tags inside <th> is invalid HTML syntax; <th> cells must be placed inside a <tr> row.

current_mapping.description: write HTML code to: a. insert an image, b. apply a border to an image, c. select width of an image, d. select height of an image, e. select an alternate text for an image;

stem:
An image with the following specifications is to be inserted in a web page.
• The name of the image is flower.jpg
• The alternative text for image is "Flower Picture"
• The width and height of the image are to be 100 pixels
• A solid black border having thickness of 3 pixels surrounds the picture

The HTML code to insert these specifications in a web page is

options.B: <alt="Flower Picture" img src="flower.jpg" width="100" height="100" style="border:3px solid black">
options.D: <style="border:3px solid black" img src="flower.jpg" alt="Flower Picture" width="100" height="100">

explanation: An HTML image element must begin with the tag name `<img` followed by the full filename including extension (`src="flower.jpg"`), `alt="Flower Picture"`, `width="100"`, `height="100"`, and `style="border:3px solid black"`.

option_feedback.reason: Option A omits the required '.jpg' file extension in src="flower", so the browser cannot locate flower.jpg.
An HTML tag must start with the element name `<img`, not an attribute like `<alt=...`.
Starting the tag with `<style=...` before `img` is invalid HTML syntax.

current_mapping.description: apply appropriate text formatting tags, i.e., bold, underline, italic, strikethrough, superscript, subscript, centre, font size, font colour and font face;

options.D: <sup>X</sup>2 + <sub>Y</sub>2

explanation: In X₂ + Y², the '2' after X is a subscript (`<sub>2</sub>`) and the '2' after Y is a superscript (`<sup>2</sup>`), giving `X<sub>2</sub> + Y<sup>2</sup>`.

option_feedback.reason: Option A swaps superscript and subscript, rendering X² + Y₂ instead of X₂ + Y².
Option C places the variables X and Y inside the subscript/superscript tags instead of the number 2.
Option D both places the variables X and Y inside the tags and swaps superscript/subscript.

current_mapping.description: apply code using inline/ internal CSS: a. background (color and image), b. font (colour, style and size), c. tables (border, size, alignment);

current_mapping.description: write a JavaScript code that uses input functions prompt( );

current_mapping.description: explain the following key concepts of data science: a. data science, b. data and dataset, c. data analysis, d. statistics and probability, e. mathematics, f. machine learning, g. deep learning, h. data mining, i. data visualisation, j. big data, k. predictive model, l. natural language processing (NLP), m. image processing;

stem: In computer science, data science contributes to

options.D: network configuration.

explanation: Data science combines statistics, mathematics, and computing to perform data analysis and uncover actionable patterns from structured and unstructured datasets.

option_feedback.reason: Hardware storage management is handled by database/storage administration rather than being the core contribution of data science.
Software deployment is a DevOps/software engineering responsibility, not the focus of data science.
Network configuration belongs to computer networking and system administration.

current_mapping.description: explain the following key concepts of data science: a. data science, b. data and dataset, c. data analysis, d. statistics and probability, e. mathematics, f. machine learning, g. deep learning, h. data mining, i. data visualisation, j. big data, k. predictive model, l. natural language processing (NLP), m. image processing;

stem: The MAIN goal of data analysis is to

options.D: sort large files.

explanation: The primary objective of data analysis is to inspect, clean, and model data in order to extract meaningful insights that support informed decision-making.

option_feedback.reason: Creating user interfaces is part of front-end UI/UX design, not data analysis.
Exporting CSV files is just a file-transfer step, not the analytical goal.
Sorting files is a basic data-organisation operation, whereas data analysis aims to discover meaningful insights.

current_mapping.description: explain the scope and application of data science;

stem:
A public health agency tracks real-time clinical reports, regional infection spikes, population density, and vaccination coverage to deploy emergency health reserves before an outbreak worsens. The response model improves year after year with updated data.

The conclusion that accurately reflects the strategic role of data science in this case is that it

options.A: forecasts resource shortages to drive policy decisions.
options.B: monitors daily staff attendance in regional hospitals.
options.D: evaluates insurance claim discrepancies.

explanation: By analysing infection spikes, population density, and vaccination coverage ahead of time, predictive data science models forecast medical resource needs and guide proactive public health policy decisions.

option_feedback.reason: Routine staff attendance tracking is basic HR record-keeping, not predictive epidemiological modelling.
Document automation is administrative clerical software, whereas the scenario describes predictive outbreak response.
The scenario focuses on deploying emergency health reserves before outbreaks worsen, not auditing insurance claims.

current_mapping.description: explain the concept of data and its types (qualitative and quantitative) emphasising their characteristics and importance;

stem:
An educational institution tracks students exam scores, attendance rates and feedback on course content and students' experiences. The scores and attendance are numerical, whereas feedback includes open-ended responses about course strengths and weaknesses.

Considering the given situation, data can be classified as

| Option | Quantitative | Qualitative |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A | exam scores | feedback responses |
| B | attendance rates | exam scores |
| C | feedback responses | students experiences |
| D | students experiences | attendance rates |

options.A: Quantitative: exam scores | Qualitative: feedback responses
options.B: Quantitative: attendance rates | Qualitative: exam scores
options.C: Quantitative: feedback responses | Qualitative: students experiences
options.D: Quantitative: students experiences | Qualitative: attendance rates

explanation: Quantitative data consists of numerical measurements (such as exam scores and attendance rates), whereas qualitative data consists of descriptive, non-numerical text (such as open-ended feedback responses and student experiences).

option_feedback.reason: Exam scores are numerical measurements and therefore belong under Quantitative data, not Qualitative data.
Open-ended feedback responses are descriptive text (Qualitative), not numerical (Quantitative).
Students' experiences are descriptive (Qualitative) and attendance rates are numerical (Quantitative), so Option D reverses both categories.

current_mapping.description: describe the following concepts of big data within the context of technology and society: a. big data, b. 3 Vs big data, c. big data analytics, d. data visualisation and interpretation;

stem: The vast amount of data generated and stored across various systems refers to one of the characteristics of big data that is

options.D: velocity.

explanation: Among the 3 Vs of Big Data (Volume, Velocity, Variety), 'Volume' refers to the massive quantity/amount of data generated and stored across systems.

option_feedback.reason: Variety refers to the different formats and types of data (structured, semi-structured, unstructured), not the sheer amount.
Validity refers to data accuracy and correctness for a given use, not the vast quantity of stored data.
Velocity refers to the speed at which new data is generated and processed in real time.

current_mapping.description: describe the following concepts of big data within the context of technology and society: a. big data, b. 3 Vs big data, c. big data analytics, d. data visualisation and interpretation;

stem: Data visualisation contributes to big data interpretation by all of the following ways EXCEPT

options.A: transforming raw data into interactive formats for decision-making.
options.B: organising data in a structured format for database integration.
options.C: relying on statistical analysis to provide direct solutions.
options.D: storing data in graphical representations for future use.

explanation: Data visualisation focuses on presenting data visually (charts, dashboards, graphs) for human interpretation; organising data into structured schemas for database integration is a database/ETL engineering task, not data visualisation.

option_feedback.reason: Transforming raw data into interactive visual dashboards for decision-making is a core function of data visualisation.
Visual analytics combines statistical summaries with visual plots to highlight patterns and solutions.
Saving graphical charts and visual reports for future reference is a standard feature of data visualisation tools.

current_mapping.description: explain the application of big data in the following business domains: a. healthcare, b. internet of things (IoT), c. manufacturing, d. government.

stem: In the government sector, big data is MOSTLY used to

options.D: monitor individual citizen activities.

explanation: Governments primarily use big data analytics across census, healthcare, economy, and infrastructure datasets to formulate evidence-based, informed public policy decisions.

option_feedback.reason: Tax tracking is only one narrow administrative function, whereas big data broadly supports public policy formulation across all sectors.
Surveillance is a specific security use case, not the primary civic purpose of government big data analytics.
Monitoring individual citizens raises privacy concerns and is not the primary developmental goal of big data in governance.

current_mapping.description: discuss the application of AI in the following fields: a. healthcare, b. robotics, c. education, d. transportation, e. entertainment, f. natural language process (NLP);

stem: Modern transportation systems benefit from Artificial Intelligence (AI) by

options.A: providing fixed schedules without live data.
options.B: delaying route updates until human approval.
options.C: suggesting routes based only on past routines.
options.D: optimising routes through traffic pattern analysis.

explanation: AI in transportation analyses real-time and historical traffic patterns, weather, and road conditions to dynamically optimise vehicle routing and reduce congestion.

option_feedback.reason: Fixed schedules without live data do not use AI's real-time adaptive capabilities.
AI navigation systems update routes automatically in real time rather than delaying for manual human approval.
Relying only on static past routines ignores live traffic bottlenecks that AI pattern analysis resolves.

current_mapping.description: discuss the application of AI in the following fields: a. healthcare, b. robotics, c. education, d. transportation, e. entertainment, f. natural language process (NLP);

stem:
A warehouse uses intelligent robots equipped with sensors and AI algorithms to navigate paths, avoid collisions and adapt routes during inventory transportation.

The robotics application of AI supports logistics by

options.A: optimising movement through real-time path correction.
options.B: repeating fixed routines regardless of surroundings.
options.C: tracking items solely through barcode timestamps.
options.D: triggering alarms based on default motion paths.

explanation: By combining sensor data with AI navigation algorithms, warehouse robots detect obstacles and dynamically adjust their paths in real time to optimise inventory movement.

option_feedback.reason: Unintelligent mechanical automation repeats fixed routines blindly, whereas AI-equipped robots adapt to their surroundings.
Passive barcode timestamp logging does not involve autonomous obstacle avoidance or route adaptation.
AI logistics robots actively reroute around obstacles rather than merely sounding alarms on fixed paths.

current_mapping.description: describe the fundamental concept of Machine Learning (ML), emphasising their importance in various fields;

stem: The role of Machine Learning (ML) in modern systems is demonstrated by

options.A: enabling systems to adapt and improve through experience-based learning.
options.B: recognizing hidden patterns in large datasets to support decision-making.
options.C: enhancing predictive accuracy through continuous data analysis.
options.D: automating complex tasks by learning from previous outcomes.

explanation: By definition (SLO 5.2.1), the fundamental concept of Machine Learning (ML) is enabling computer systems to automatically learn, adapt, and improve from experience without being explicitly reprogrammed.

option_feedback.reason: Recognizing hidden patterns in large datasets describes data mining specifically rather than the core definition of ML adaptation.
Enhancing predictive accuracy through data analysis describes predictive analytics, which is one outcome of ML.
Task automation is an application benefit, whereas enabling systems to adapt and improve through experience is the foundational role of ML.

current_mapping.description: describe the following types of machine learning (ML): a. supervised learning, b. unsupervised learning, c. reinforcement learning;

stem: A robot learns to navigate by receiving rewards or penalties using

options.A: reinforcement learning based on environmental interaction.
options.B: unsupervised learning driven by hidden data patterns.
options.C: supervised learning based on static labeled training.
options.D: machine learning with curated instructions.

explanation: Reinforcement learning is the type of Machine Learning in which an agent (such as a robot) interacts with an environment and learns optimal actions through trial-and-error rewards and penalties.

option_feedback.reason: Unsupervised learning clusters unlabelled data by hidden similarity patterns without using reward/penalty signals.
Supervised learning trains models on pre-labelled input-output pairs rather than environmental rewards and penalties.
Curated step-by-step instructions describe traditional rule-based programming, not reward-based learning.

current_mapping.description: explain the following applications of cloud computing: a. software development, b. data analytics, c. IoT (Internet of Things).

stem: Cloud platforms support software development by

options.A: restricting access to pre-installed coding templates.
options.B: enabling scalable collaboration across remote teams.
options.C: removing the need for any development tools entirely.
options.D: executing local programs through static environments.

explanation: Cloud computing provides on-demand, scalable development environments, shared code repositories, and CI/CD pipelines that allow remote software teams to collaborate seamlessly.

option_feedback.reason: Cloud platforms expand access to shared templates, libraries, and services rather than restricting them.
Software development still requires coding, testing, and debugging tools, which cloud platforms host online.
Executing purely local programs on static machines is traditional on-premise computing, not cloud computing.

current_mapping.description: illustrate the role of computing in the following fields by demonstrating real-world applications and examples: a. healthcare, b. education, c. business, d. entertainment;

stem:
An educational platform integrates voice recognition to help learners with reading disabilities improve pronunciation.

The given scenario illustrates computing used for developing

options.D: visual skills.

explanation: Helping learners read aloud and improve spoken pronunciation directly develops their verbal and reading 'language skills'.

option_feedback.reason: Psychomotor skills involve physical hand-eye coordination and motor movement, not word pronunciation.
Voice recognition evaluates the learner's spoken pronunciation (speaking/reading), not passive listening.
Visual skills involve interpreting images or spatial graphics rather than vocal pronunciation.

current_mapping.description: explain the following cyber security threats: a. brute force attacks, b. denial of services (DoS), c. distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, d. trojan horse, e. spyware, f. adware, g. phishing, h. pharming, i. social engineering;

stem: Brute force attacks take place by

options.A: trying many password combinations until access is gained.
options.B: sending malware through flash drives into secure systems.
options.C: pretending to be a trusted user through deceptive emails.
options.D: influencing users to download false applications.

explanation: A brute force attack uses automated scripts to systematically test thousands or millions of possible password/key combinations until the correct credential is found.

option_feedback.reason: Spreading malware via infected USB flash drives is physical media malware transmission, not a brute force attack.
Pretending to be a trusted entity via deceptive emails is phishing.
Tricking users into installing fake software is a Trojan horse / social engineering attack.

current_mapping.description: explain the following methods to protect data from security threats: a. access levels, b. anti-malware, c. authentication (passwords and usernames, biometrics, two step verification).

stem: Two-step verification improves security by

options.A: encrypting all personal information at once.
options.B: creating backup files during login procedures.
options.C: using a single password for more than one platform.
options.D: applying more than one method other than a password.

explanation: Two-step verification (2FA) strengthens authentication by requiring a second verification factor (such as an OTP code or biometric check) in addition to the user's password.

option_feedback.reason: File encryption protects stored data confidentiality, whereas two-step verification is an authentication control during login.
Creating data backups protects against data loss, not unauthorized account login.
Reusing a single password across multiple platforms weakens security and is the opposite of strong authentication.

current_mapping.description: explain entrepreneurship and its importance in the economy;

stem: An essential role of entrepreneurs in the economy involves

options.B: avoiding financial risks at every opportunity.
options.C: identifying gaps to offer innovative solutions.
options.D: delaying product launches to avoid competition.

explanation: Entrepreneurs drive economic growth by spotting unmet consumer needs or market gaps and creating innovative products, services, or digital ventures to solve them.

option_feedback.reason: Entrepreneurs disrupt outdated models with better innovations rather than merely promoting all existing business models.
Entrepreneurship inherently involves taking calculated financial and operational risks rather than avoiding all risk.
Entrepreneurs compete actively by bringing timely solutions to market rather than delaying launches out of fear of competition.

current_mapping.description: explain market trends, consumer needs, and emerging industries of entrepreneurship;

stem: Market trends in entrepreneurship typically refer to the

options.B: consumers’ preferences for a specific brand.
options.C: government’s regulation to prevent market shifts.
options.D: traditional practices that do not change over time.

explanation: Market trends reflect the directional shift and evolution/modification of products, technologies, and industry offerings over time in response to changing market demands.

option_feedback.reason: Preference for a single specific brand is brand loyalty, whereas a market trend spans an entire industry over time.
Government regulations are legal policies, not market trends.
Static traditional practices that never change are the opposite of dynamic market trends.

current_mapping.description: apply various idea generation techniques to identify business opportunities in the digital space;

stem:
A tech startup explores building AI chatbots for e-commerce platforms. They list common chatbot limitations and explore possibilities to replace, combine, adapt and modify functionalities to deliver better performance.

Based on the given scenario, the technique for generating innovative chatbot ideas is

options.A: SWOT to assess internal financial risks.
options.B: reverse engineering to reduce bot speed.
options.D: trend analysis to copy what’s already successful.

explanation: SCAMPER (Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Reverse) is the structured ideation technique that systematically replaces, combines, adapts, and modifies existing product features to generate innovative improvements.

option_feedback.reason: SWOT analysis evaluates Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats rather than replacing, combining, and adapting product features.
Reverse engineering deconstructs an existing product to understand its design, not to reduce speed.
Trend analysis studies market direction rather than applying the SCAMPER feature-modification prompts.
